build_tactics: Plants itself between the enemy and everyone squishier and simply does not move. Its damage is modest; its job is that every swing aimed at it misses and every path around it costs an attack of opportunity.

boons_detail.description: (Pairs with Draining Casting) You shore up your lifeforce against draining magic; you may use Constitution as your casting ability modifier if it is higher than your usual one.
boons_detail.name: Fortified Casting

boons_detail.description: Your sphere abilities are more potent; for example, while your current spell points are at half your total or less you gain +1 caster level, rising to +2 at 0 spell points.
boons_detail.name: Empowered Abilities

drawbacks_detail.description: Your magic requires elaborate gestures; you need a free hand and suffer arcane-style spell failure in armor heavier than light. May be taken twice (no armor or shield at all without failure).
drawbacks_detail.name: Somatic Casting

drawbacks_detail.description: Your magic is addictive; each time you spend spell points you must make an escalating Fortitude save or risk gaining/intensifying an addiction, taking escalating penalties until you cast again.
drawbacks_detail.name: Addictive Casting

drawbacks_detail.description: Your magic requires expending consumable materials/components worth roughly 1 sp per caster level each time you use a sphere ability.
drawbacks_detail.name: Material Casting

drawbacks_detail.description: Your magic is channeled through an activity tied to a specific Craft, Perform, or Profession skill; you must succeed on a skill check (DC 15 + the ability's caster level) for any sphere ability to take effect.
drawbacks_detail.name: Skilled Casting

Actions.10 E-Kats: hero point: Use as a Hero Point (you can store it if you have room).
Actions.2 E-Kats: bonus: Gain a +1 on ANY roll; +2 if declared before the roll.
Actions.2 E-Kats: penalty: Inflict a -1 on ANY roll; -2 if declared before the roll.
Actions.20 E-Kats: borrow a feat or spell: Gain the ability to use a feat or mythic spell you qualify for, excluding the mythic requirement. Feats last one minute; spells last for the duration of the spell.
Actions.25 E-Kats: Luck Trait: 25 permanent E-Kats can be used to purchase a Luck Trait.
Actions.5 E-Kats: stabilize: Stabilize ANYONE within five feet, provided they are not already beyond stabilization.
Actions.99 E-Kats: Destined Template: Gain the "Destined" Template (only once per player). This action locks your slot into a future campaign and ties it to this character.
Actions.99 E-Kats: survive anything: You may exchange 99 E-Kats to survive anything.
Actions.Hero point for 5 E-Kats: 1 non-temporary Hero Point can be exchanged for 5 E-Kats (not multiplied by Lucky Boy).

Feats Not Taken (reference).Feat: Luck God: [+4 Luck] All E-Kat costs (excluding the 99 tier and purchasing new Luck Traits) are cut in half; you gain a +2 bonus to all saves, attacks, ability checks, skill checks, AC, and Caster Level Checks. You gain a +4 Luck, and once per day can force a reroll in your favor.
Feats Not Taken (reference).Feat: Lucky Boy: [+1 Luck] E-Kat (roll based) bonuses are doubled.
Feats Not Taken (reference).Feat: Middle Finger: [+1 Luck] Gain 1 E-Kat anytime the GM has a hostile NPC utilize a Hero Point.
Feats Not Taken (reference).Feat: Stream of Luck: [+1 Luck] Gain one E-Kat per session (character played), two if you have Double Down.
Feats Not Taken (reference).Feat: Sweet Dreams: [+1 Luck] Gain one E-Kat per in-game long rest, two if you have Double Down. (Applies once to timeskips longer than a day.)
Feats Not Taken (reference).Feat: Very Lucky Boy: [+1 Luck] E-Kat (roll based) bonuses are increased to triple.

Feats Taken.Feat: Ass Pull: [+4 Luck] Gain 4 E-Kats per session that expire upon the session's end, and a +4 Luck.
Feats Taken.Feat: It Just Works: [+4 Luck] Gain one free Hero Point per session that expires upon the session's end, +4 Luck.
Feats Taken.Feat: Right of Deferment: [+1 Luck] You may wait to apply E-Kats after a roll for no penalty.

Reserve.Your reserve: 15 E-Kat(s) carried into play, of 15 earned at creation (0 spent on Luck Traits at 25 each). Storage cap 99.

Skill Unlock: Bluff.10 Ranks: You take no penalty to Bluff a creature after a failed check unless you failed by 5 or more.
Skill Unlock: Bluff.15 Ranks: Creatures magically attempting to read your thoughts, detect your alignment, or reveal when you are lying must succeed at a caster level check (DC 11 + your Bluff ranks) or the effect reveals nothing.
Skill Unlock: Bluff.20 Ranks: As a full-round action you can make a suggestion (as the spell, max 1 hour) to a creature within 30 feet (Will negates, DC 15 + Cha mod). This is an extraordinary mind-affecting compulsion.
Skill Unlock: Bluff.5 Ranks: The penalty to Bluff a creature after a failed check is halved unless you failed by 5 or more.

armored master.description: the fighter gains an armor mastery feat or a shield mastery feat as a bonus feat. He must meet all of the feats prerequisites.

unmoving (ex).description: select one combat maneuver (except sunder). Whether using his armor as leverage against a grappling foe or using its weight to help him stop a bull rush, a fighter can use his armor to protect him from the chosen combat maneuver. While wearing armor or wielding a shield, the fighter gains a bonus to his cmd against the chosen combat maneuver. The bonus is +1 if hes wearing light armor, +2 if hes wearing medium armor, and +3 if hes wearing heavy armor. This bonus increases by 1 at 7th level and every 4 fighter levels thereafter, to a maximum at 19th level of +5 for light armor, +6 for medium armor, and +7 for heavy armor. Mithral armor provides a bonus 1 lower than normal for armor of its type.

versatile training (ex).description: the fighter can use his base attack bonus in place of his ranks in two skills of his choice that are associated with the fighter weapon group he has chosen with this option.

class_ability_desc.armor mastery: At 19th level, a fighter gains DR 5/- whenever he is wearing armor or using a shield.
class_ability_desc.armor training: Starting at 3rd level, a fighter learns to be more maneuverable while wearing armor. Whenever he is wearing armor, he reduces the armor check penalty by 1 (to a minimum of 0) and increases the maximum Dexterity bonus allowed by his armor by 1. Every four levels thereafter (7th, 11th, and 15th), these bonuses increase by +1 each time, to a maximum -4 reduction of the armor check penalty and a +4 increase of the maximum Dexterity bonus allowed. In addition, a fighter can also move at his normal speed while wearing medium armor. At 7th level, a fighter can move at his normal speed while wearing heavy armor.
class_ability_desc.bonus feats: At 1st level, and at every even level thereafter, a fighter gains a bonus feat in addition to those gained from normal advancement (meaning that the fighter gains a feat at every level). These bonus feats must be selected from those listed as combat feats, sometimes also called "fighter bonus feats."Upon reaching 4th level, and every four levels thereafter (8th, 12th, and so on), a fighter can choose to learn a new bonus feat in place of a bonus feat he has already learned. In effect, the fighter loses the bonus feat in exchange for the new one. The old feat cannot be one that was used as a prerequisite for another feat, prestige class, or other ability. A fighter can only change one feat at any given level and must choose whether or not to swap the feat at the time he gains a new bonus feat for the level.
class_ability_desc.bravery: Starting at 2nd level, a fighter gains a +1 bonus on Will saves against fear. This bonus increases by +1 for every four levels beyond 2nd.
class_ability_desc.weapon mastery: At 20th level, a fighter chooses one weapon, such as the longsword, greataxe, or longbow. Any attacks made with that weapon automatically confirm all critical threats and have their damage multiplier increased by 1 (×2 becomes ×3, for example). In addition, he cannot be disarmed while wielding a weapon of this type. Alternate Capstones
class_ability_desc.weapon training: Starting at 5th level, a fighter can select one group of weapons, as noted below. Whenever he attacks with a weapon from this group, he gains a +1 bonus on attack and damage rolls. Every four levels thereafter (9th, 13th, and 17th), a fighter becomes further trained in another group of weapons. He gains a +1 bonus on attack and damage rolls when using a weapon from this group. In addition, the bonuses granted by previous weapon groups increase by +1 each. For example, when a fighter reaches 9th level, he receives a +1 bonus on attack and damage rolls with one weapon group and a +2 bonus on attack and damage rolls with the weapon group selected at 5th level. Bonuses granted from overlapping groups do not stack. Take the highest bonus granted for a weapon if it resides in two or more groups. A fighter also adds this bonus to any combat maneuver checks made with weapons from this group. This bonus also applies to the fighter's Combat Maneuver Defense when defending against disarm and sunder attempts made against weapons from this group. Weapon groups are defined as follows (GMs may add other weapons to these groups, or add entirely new groups): Note from Nethys : A consolidated list of fighter weapon groups is provided here

Shielded Fighter.active defense (ex): At 3rd level, a shielded fighter gains a +1 dodge bonus to AC when wielding a shield and fighting defensively, using Combat Expertise, or using total defense. This bonus increases by +1 for every four levels beyond 3rd. As a swift action, he may share this bonus with one adjacent ally, or half of the bonus (minimum +0) with all adjacent allies, until the beginning of his next turn. This ability replaces armor training 1, 2, 3, and 4.
Shielded Fighter.shield buffet (ex): At 9th level, as a move action, a shielded fighter may make a combat maneuver check to use his shield to impede an adjacent enemy. If successful, the target suffers a -2 penalty on its attack rolls against the shielded fighter and a -2 penalty to AC on attacks made by the shielded fighter until the beginning of his next turn. At 13th level, a shielded fighter may use this ability as a swift action. This ability replaces weapon training 2 and 3.
Shielded Fighter.shield fighter (ex): At 5th level, a shielded fighter gains a +1 bonus on attack and damage rolls when making a shield bash. These bonuses increase by +1 every four levels beyond 5th. With a full attack action, a shielded fighter may alternate between using his weapon or his shield for each attack. This action does not grant additional attacks or incur penalties as two-weapon fighting does. This ability replaces weapon training 1.
Shielded Fighter.shield guard (ex): At 17th level, as a swift action, a shielded fighter may designate one square adjacent to him. He may designate two squares if using a heavy shield or three squares if using a tower shield, but these squares must be contiguous. Enemies in these squares cannot flank the shielded fighter and do not count for flanking with other creatures. This effect lasts until he moves from his position or uses another swift action to change the affected squares. This ability replaces weapon training 4.
Shielded Fighter.shield mastery (ex): At 19th level, a shielded fighter gains DR 5/- when wielding a shield. This ability replaces armor mastery.
Shielded Fighter.shield ward (ex): At 20th level, a shielded fighter gains evasion (as a rogue) while wielding a shield, and adds his shield bonus to his AC (not including enhancement bonuses) on Reflex saves and to his touch AC. In addition, his shield cannot be disarmed or sundered. This ability replaces weapon mastery.
Shielded Fighter.source: Advanced Player's Guide pg. 108 A shielded fighter focuses on both offense and defense, blending weapon and shield in perfect balance to impede his enemies while delivering deadly blows, and even turning the shield itself into a formidable weapon. These fighting school benefits apply when wielding a weapon and a shield simultaneously.

combat_talent_items.description: If you are using a shield and you are attacked by a creature you are aware of while not flat-footed, you may spend an attack of opportunity to increase your shield bonus to AC against that attack by +2. This decision must be made before the roll is made. For every 4 points of base attack bonus you possess, the increase to your shield bonus provided by this talent increases by 1. Talents with the (deflect) tag grant additional effects to this ability. Each use of active defense may only benefit from one (deflect) talent. You may expend your martial focus to use active defense in place of spending an attack of opportunity.
combat_talent_items.name: Active Defense

combat_talent_items.description:
As long as you have martial focus, you may use active defense to benefit an ally when an ally within your shield's reach is targeted by an attack.

Note: This only provides the benefits of active defense, not the benefit of the base shield. (Source)
combat_talent_items.name: Cover Ally

combat_talent_items.description:
When you use your active defense, you may choose to make an attack roll as if making a shield bash and must use the result of this attack in place of your AC for resolving the attack, even if lower. You must be capable of making shield bash attacks with the shield to use this ability.

Note: Punch Block replaces your entire AC bonus with your attack roll; treat this as though using your active defense. This is not a shield bonus, and does not apply to attacks which would bypass your Shield bonus (such as the Improved Precise Shot feat). The Deflecting Shield talent does not allow Punch Block to apply against touch attacks.
combat_talent_items.name: Punch Block

combat_talent_items.description: You may expend martial focus as a free action that can be taken even when it's not your turn to apply your active defense against all valid triggering attacks until the start of your next turn without spending attacks of opportunity. If you possess the Cover Ally talent, you may apply this benefit to all allies within reach.
combat_talent_items.name: Extensive Defense

combat_talent_items.description: You do not lose your shield bonus to AC when making an attack with your shield. Additionally, you may make shield bash attacks with a buckler as if it were a light shield. Reduce the damage as if the shield bash was one size smaller when used this way. Associated Feat: Improved Shield Bash.
combat_talent_items.name: Bashing Shield

combat_talent_items.description: Your shield bonus to AC applies against touch attacks.
combat_talent_items.name: Deflecting Shield

combat_talent_items.description: Whenever you take the total defense action while wielding a shield, creatures that miss you provoke attacks of opportunity from you. You may make these attacks of opportunity but take a penalty on the attack rolls as if you were fighting defensively.
combat_talent_items.name: Reactive Defense

combat_talent_items.description: You may spend an immediate action to redirect the damage from a successful attack against you to your shield. This action is taken after the result of the attack roll is known but before the damage is revealed. Attacks that do not target you directly or which do not deal hit point damage cannot be redirected in this manner.
combat_talent_items.name: Sacrificial Shield

combat_talent_items.description:
While wielding a buckler, shield, or tower shield, you may spend a move action to regain your martial focus whenever you choose to fight defensively as part of an attack action.

Additionally, whenever an attack misses a creature benefiting from your active defense, you may regain your martial focus as an immediate action.
combat_talent_items.name: Shielded Focus

combat_talent_items.description: Creatures benefiting from your active defense bonus (including yourself) gain DR/- equal to the bonus from active defense against attacks that hit despite active defense. This damage reduction stacks with damage reduction from other sources.
combat_talent_items.name: Interposing Shield

combat_talent_items.description: Whenever an attack misses a creature benefiting from your active defense, you may spend an immediate action to release a burst of energy, dealing damage as if you had made a successful shield bash to all enemies within a 15-foot cone (or a 10-foot radius burst), centered on the initial target. Creatures within the area may attempt a Reflex saving throw to negate this damage.
combat_talent_items.name: Quaking Block

belts.description: this belt's golden buckle depicts a bear's head. The belt grants the wearer an enhancement bonus to constitution of +2, +4, or +6. Treat this as a temporary ability bonus for the first 24 hours the belt is worn.

body.description: the cut and color of this solemn vestment varies from religion to religion, but its properties are the same. The wearer may command the cassock of the clergy to display the holy symbol of her deity or hide this symbol. At the most basic level, the garment functions as a divine focus. Additionally, the wearer gains a +3 competence bonus on charisma-based checks to influence creatures that match her alignment or that of her patron deity. Also, the wearer may use bless and sanctuary (dc 11) each once per day, and may prepare one additional orison each day. If the wearer is a spontaneous divine caster,  once per day she may spend 1 hour in prayer to gain an orison of her choice as a spell known for the next 24 hours.

chest.description: this tight-fitting garment of fine silk has thin bone ribbing sewn into it. Once per day as a move action, the wearer can take an additional swift action. This swift action can't be used to cast a spell or spell-like ability. The shirt must be worn for 24 hours before this ability can be used.

eyes.description: these spectacles fit firmly over eyes and are held in place by two crystalline stems. The lenses are initially clear and don't hinder the wearer's vision. When the wearer is targeted with an illusion spell or spell-like ability of the pattern subschool (such as color spray), the spectacles absorb the magic and darken, protecting the wearer from the pattern effect. Once the spectacles absorb a spell and become opaque, the wearer becomes blinded until the spectacles are removed (a swift action). Patternward spectacles protect against spells or spell-like abilities of only 3rd level or lower; higher-level effects affect the wearer as normal. Once the spectacles absorb an effect, they lose their magic.

hands.description: the wearer of these simple gloves can speak a command word create a glowing disembodied hand. As a swift action, the wearer can have the hand assist him with a task as if using the aid another action.  the hand uses the wearer's base attack bonus or skill ranks when making the check to see if aid another is successful (it does not gain the benefit of the wearer's ability scores or other bonuses). The hand remains until it has attempted one action or until 1 minute passes, whichever comes first, at which time the gloves become nonmagical.

head.description: this conical iron jingasa, or war hat, grants the wearer a +1 deflection bonus to ac. When struck by a critical hit or sneak attack, the wearer can spend an immediate action to negate the critical hit or sneak attack (similar to the fortification armor special ability, but without requiring a roll). The damage is instead rolled normally.  this ability functions only once, though the jingasa continues to grant its deflection bonus even after the other ability is expended.

neck.description: this amulet, usually containing some type of magically preserved monster hide or other natural armorsuch as bone, horn, carapace, or beast scales toughens the wearer's body and flesh,  giving him an enhancement bonus to his natural armor from +1 to +5,  depending on the kind of amulet.

rings.description: This ring offers continual magical protection in the form of a deflection bonus of +1 to +5 to AC.

shoulders.description: flecks of silver or steel are often sown amid the fabric of these magical cloaks. This garment offers magical protection in the form of a +1 to +5 resistance bonus on all saving throws (fortitude, reflex, and will).

wrist.description: these translucent cloth tubes easily fit over their wearer's arms. The wearer of these sleeves can, when she slips them on, choose to transform the appearance of her current garments into any other nonmagical set of clothing. These new clothes fit her perfectly and are always clean and mended unless she specifically designates otherwise. When she removes the sleeves, her clothes revert to their original form.

contextNotes.text: While fighting defensively or using total defense: the fighting-defensively attack penalty is only -2, and you gain an additional +1 dodge bonus to AC.
+1 shield bonus to AC while using Snapping Turtle Style with at least one hand free
+1 shield bonus to AC while wielding a double weapon or two weapons; increases to +2 while fighting defensively or using total defense.

Crane Style.name: Crane Style: Effect: fighting defensively costs only [[-2]] on attack rolls instead of the normal penalty, and grants an additional +[[1]] dodge bonus to AC while fighting defensively or using total defense

contextNotes.text: Bespectacled: -[[20]] Perception when not wearing glasses.

Bespectacled.description: Without your glasses the world is a smear of color. You take a -20 penalty on Perception checks when not wearing your glasses.

contextNotes.text: Insomniac: each morning, [[20]]% chance to start the day fatigued.

Insomniac.description: You have trouble achieving a full and restful sleep. Each morning there is a 20% chance you begin the day fatigued until you next get a full night's rest.

formatted_bio:
Alice Gagné
- Alignment: Lawful Good
- Deity: Iomedae
- Race: Orc
- Class: Level 11 Fighter
- Archetype: AC Tank
- Tactics: Plants itself between the enemy and everyone squishier and simply does not move. Its damage is modest; its job is that every swing aimed at it misses and every path around it costs an attack of opportunity.
- Stat Focus: Str
- Homeland: Tal-falko

Vocation
- Profession: Royal Envoy (rank 1)
- Profession: Ironmonger (rank 1)
- Profession: Hearthmaster (rank 10)
- Profession: Alley Caper (rank 4)
- Profession: Magician (rank 10)
- Known for: Bookbinding

Family
- Absent Mother
- Dead Father
- Adopted Into A Middle Income Family
- 1 Younger Brother
- 2 Younger Sisters

Personality
- Personality: Idiosyncratic, Contemplative, Attentive, Ambitious
- Mannerisms: Twists hair, Jingles keys, Brushes hair out of face, Covers ears
- Flaws: Insomniac, Bespectacled

Appearance
- Hair: Spiky Brown
- Eyes: Amber
- Build: Plump

Talents gained:
- Reactive Defense (Shield): Whenever you take the total defense action while wielding a shield, creatures that miss you provoke attacks of opportunity from you. You may make these attacks of opportunity but take a penalty on the attack rolls as if you were fighting defensively.
- Sacrificial Shield (Shield): You may spend an immediate action to redirect the damage from a successful attack against you to your shield. This action is taken after the result of the attack roll is known but before the damage is revealed. Attacks that do not target you directly or which do not deal hit point damage cannot be r
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Extra Combat Talent (Shielded Focus / In:
Extra Combat Talent > Extra Combat Talent (house rule: one slot, two talents).
Talents gained:
- Shielded Focus (Shield): While wielding a buckler, shield, or tower shield, you may spend a move action to regain your martial focus whenever you choose to fight defensively as part of an attack action.  Additionally, whenever an attack misses a creature benefiting from your active defense, you may regain your martial focus
- Interposing Shield (Shield): Creatures benefiting from your active defense bonus (including yourself) gain DR/- equal to the bonus from active defense against attacks that hit despite active defense. This damage reduction stacks with damage reduction from other sources.

profession_ability_items.description:
Profession (Hearthmaster) - rank 10/10. Associate skills (ranks 1/4/7/10): Knowledge (local), Handle Animal, Craft, Sense Motive.

Larder Keeper (Ex)

The pantry is deep and well organized. The character gains a +2 competence bonus on Profession (cook) and Survival checks made to provide food and water for others.

Honest Welcome (Ex)

A reputation for fair dealing precedes this innkeeper. They gain a +2 competence bonus on all Diplomacy checks.

Warming Hearth (Ex)

The common-room fire is kept high and bright, and the character knows how to settle frayed nerves. Allies who rest near them for one hour gain a +1 morale bonus on saves against fear for the next hour.
profession_ability_items.name: Profession Rank 5: (Hearthmaster)

profession_ability_items.description:
Profession (Magician) - rank 10/10. Associate skills (ranks 1/4/7/10): Sense Motive, Craft, Profession, Use Magic Device.

Scholar's Insight (Ex)

Years bent over grimoires sharpen the Fighter's recall of arcane lore. They gain a +2 competence bonus on Knowledge (arcana) checks, and may always take 10 on Knowledge (arcana) even when distracted or threatened.

Apprentice Spellcasting (Sp)

Choose two spells of 1st or 2nd level from the wizard/sorcerer spell list (such as mage armor, shield, or magic missile). You can cast each twice per day as a spell-like ability (caster level equal to your character level).

Mage Armor (Sp)

Once per day the Fighter can sheathe themselves in mage armor, conjuring a tangible field of force that wards off blows for the better part of a day.
profession_ability_items.name: Profession Rank 5: (Magician)

unlock.10: You take no penalty to Bluff a creature after a failed check unless you failed by 5 or more.
unlock.15: Creatures magically attempting to read your thoughts, detect your alignment, or reveal when you are lying must succeed at a caster level check (DC 11 + your Bluff ranks) or the effect reveals nothing.
unlock.20: As a full-round action you can make a suggestion (as the spell, max 1 hour) to a creature within 30 feet (Will negates, DC 15 + Cha mod). This is an extraordinary mind-affecting compulsion.
unlock.5: The penalty to Bluff a creature after a failed check is halved unless you failed by 5 or more.

skill_unlock.unlock_html:
Bluff

5 Ranks: The penalty to Bluff a creature after a failed check is halved unless you failed by 5 or more.

10 Ranks: You take no penalty to Bluff a creature after a failed check unless you failed by 5 or more.

15 Ranks: Creatures magically attempting to read your thoughts, detect your alignment, or reveal when you are lying must succeed at a caster level check (DC 11 + your Bluff ranks) or the effect reveals nothing.

20 Ranks: As a full-round action you can make a suggestion (as the spell, max 1 hour) to a creature within 30 feet (Will negates, DC 15 + Cha mod). This is an extraordinary mind-affecting compulsion.
